site.heroSubtitle: Senior fullstack dev, ~9 years of XP, embedded software background. I code alongside PMs and designers, and I like to look at the numbers before touching the code.

depart.title: Start
depart.description: Two years in HealthTech. Internship on chatbots, then fullstack dev on e-health apps (Angular, Java/Spring, MySQL). That's where I picked up the basics of CI/CD and SCRUM. After two years, time to see how things were done elsewhere.

expansion.title: Expansion
expansion.description: Off to Birmingham to rebuild the PM Connect website (HTML/SCSS/JS, PHP/Symfony, Docker, Kanban). My first startup, my first international team, and English all day long was a personal milestone as much as a professional one.

aujourdhui.title: Today
aujourdhui.description: Six years at Sencrop, in AgTech. I built and led the Growth team, then the Sales Impact team to push revenue up and churn down. On the product side, I owned the QA and production-tracking app for our 4G stations: from the sensor test bench in the factory all the way through to integration in the agricultural weather app. I also contribute to the design system, now used by three teams. Tech-wise: TypeScript everywhere (React, NestJS, GraphQL), web and native via Capacitor, Terraform infra.

passions.title: Passions
passions.subtitle: Outside of code: travel in Latin America, home automation, and quite a few different sports.

sport.title: Sports & outdoors
sport.closing: Solo or with people, depends on the day.

side-projects.title: Side projects
side-projects.closing: My "that'd be handy if..." thoughts that end up printed.

intro.title: Who I am
intro.content: Florian, senior fullstack dev, with an embedded software background to start with. I like pairing with PMs and designers, understanding what users actually want, and looking at metrics before diving into code.

sport.title: Sports & outdoors
sport.content: Road cycling, running, padel, mountain hikes. When I need to clear my head, cycling wins. Otherwise padel for something more intense.

side-projects.title: Home automation & 3D printing
side-projects.content: At home, Home Assistant runs the lights, temperature and CO2 sensors. On the side, the 3D printer mostly cranks out small everyday tools: toothbrush holders, mini battery storage, and all those "this'd be handy if..." ideas you end up modeling. That's often where I learn the most.

voyage.title: Travel
voyage.content: An obsession with the Americas (Brazil, Colombia, Guatemala, Belize) that started by accident, with a few side trips through Asia (Malaysia, India). Two moments stuck with me: tuk-tuk to the Taj Mahal in 40°C heat — passing a Kanwariya procession on the way, Shiva pilgrims carrying water from the Ganges over miles, music blaring and water poles balanced on shoulders, and Comuna 13 in Medellín, visited with a local guide who had seen the neighborhood go from the worst to a tourist spot. All my photos are shot on iPhone, and recycled all over this site — hero, backgrounds, and a couple of hidden spots.

stack.opinion: Capacitor served me well for 6 years in production at Sencrop. For a new mobile project, I'd go with React Native or Expo.

nodeDescriptions.react: My main UI library — I've built dozens of React projects since 2018.
nodeDescriptions.nextjs: React framework I know well — App Router, SSR, RSC. Used on several personal and pro projects.
nodeDescriptions.typescript: On every project since 2019. Once you switch to strict types, going back to plain JS is impossible.
nodeDescriptions.vite: Ultra-fast bundler I use on projects that aren't on Next.js.
nodeDescriptions.angular: Used on enterprise projects for 2 years. I know the ecosystem but I prefer React.
nodeDescriptions.scss: Used before Tailwind — I know how to use it but I don't go back.
nodeDescriptions.styled-components: CSS-in-JS used daily on professional projects.
nodeDescriptions.gatsbyjs: React static site generator — used for showcase sites before adopting Next.js.
nodeDescriptions.capacitor: Shipped hybrid iOS/Android apps from existing React codebases.
nodeDescriptions.capacitor-plugin: Custom native plugins to fill gaps for business needs.
nodeDescriptions.bitrise: Mobile CI/CD set up for iOS and Android builds.
nodeDescriptions.nodejs: My main backend runtime. REST APIs, workers, scripts — Node is everywhere in my stack.
nodeDescriptions.nestjs: Well-structured for big APIs: modules, guards, interceptors. When you're a few people on the codebase, it helps.
nodeDescriptions.express: The Node.js classic — used on many projects before NestJS.
nodeDescriptions.graphql: GraphQL APIs with Apollo Server and Client. Schemas, resolvers, subscriptions.
nodeDescriptions.python-fastapi: Used for data microservices and lightweight Python APIs.
nodeDescriptions.kafka: Basics only. I've consumed and produced messages in production, but without managing the stack myself.
nodeDescriptions.postgresql: My default database. Handles the load, and the Postgres docs are still the reference.
nodeDescriptions.mysql: Used on legacy projects, I prefer PostgreSQL.
nodeDescriptions.drizzle: Lighter than Prisma, better typed. I'm adopting it on new personal projects.
nodeDescriptions.prisma: Well-typed ORM, used on NestJS before Drizzle.
nodeDescriptions.terraform: Infrastructure as Code to provision reproducible AWS environments.
nodeDescriptions.docker: Systematic containerization. Multi-stage Dockerfiles, compose, registries. Used both personally and at work.
nodeDescriptions.github-actions: CI/CD pipelines on all my repos — tests, lint, automated deploys.
nodeDescriptions.aws: Lambda, S3, CloudFront, RDS, ECS, ECR, Route 53, etc. — the classic blocks for serverless and hosting.
nodeDescriptions.datadog: Monitoring and alerting in production — dashboards, APM, centralized logs.
nodeDescriptions.nix: Reproducible dev environments with devenv — I'm trying to use it everywhere.
nodeDescriptions.hubspot: CRM integration via API — contact sync, deals, automated workflows.
nodeDescriptions.chargebee: Subscription management and billing via API and webhooks.
nodeDescriptions.mixpanel: Product analytics — event tracking, funnels, retention.
nodeDescriptions.intercom: Widget integration and APIs for in-app customer support.
nodeDescriptions.contentful: Headless CMS — content models, GraphQL API, publication webhooks.
nodeDescriptions.tdd: Test-Driven Development applied daily — red/green/refactor for reliable code.
nodeDescriptions.ddd: Domain-Driven Design — bounded contexts, aggregates, ubiquitous language to model the business.
nodeDescriptions.hexagonal: Ports & Adapters — decoupling business domain from technical dependencies.
nodeDescriptions.cqrs: Read/write separation for scalable, maintainable systems.
nodeDescriptions.clean-architecture: Layered structuring with dependency inversion — business code isolated and testable.
nodeDescriptions.microservices: Splitting into autonomous services communicating via API and events — deployed independently.
